blocking.issue: This regression was introduced when L3-6 was fixed. The VM alternative says that splitting 90% of VM memory between both `ruralzd` processes only halves each C_cap. Under the document's own M_flood, most of the floor does not depend on C_cap. Any C_cap of 80 or more gives min(I_max, C_cap × 250) = 20,000, so the unit term alone is 6,250 MiB. For Example 1, M_fix + M_rej + units + Upstream come to 1,245 + 500 + 6,250 + 469 = 8,464 MiB (hypothesis). That is above the 0.45 × 13,312 = 5,990 MiB each process would get, even at C_cap = 0. An operator who takes this MAY is OOM-killed during a header or stream flood in mid-Drain, which is the failure the 2 × container row prevents. L1-1 raised the same defect.
blocking.evidence: "Operators MAY instead split 90% of VM memory between both processes' `GOMEMLIMIT` (target), halving each C_cap."; Formulas: "M_flood = M_fix + m_route × R + P_plg + (K + 2) × s_snap + M_rej + C_cap × m_c" / "+ min(I_max, C_cap × n_str) × m_u + min(I_max, Σ_u maxConnections_u) × m_up  (hypothesis)"; Capacity model prose: "80 connections can hold all 20,000 units (target): an L4 connection cap alone does not bound memory".
blocking.fix: Delete the MAY sentence, or restate it as a condition: a split is allowed only when each process's `GOMEMLIMIT` is at least M_flood at its own C_cap, which no example meets while I_max is fixed at 20,000 units. So until OQ-capacity-planning-5 lowers the unit or stream ceiling, VM hosts MUST provide 2 × container (hypothesis). Add a pointer from OQ-capacity-planning-5's question to this case.
